1. PREMISE: Your framing treats the sequence of her statements as the primary problem requiring resolution. The hidden assumption is that establishing what physically occurred that night will determine whether the relationship is viable. The analysis turns on recognizing that her pattern of concealment, revised accounts, and inability to account for her own conduct has already destroyed the informational foundation on which your continued partnership depends—regardless of what happened in that bed.

2. STAKES: Your partner stands to lose the relationship and the life you have constructed together if you conclude her conduct was deceptive. You stand to lose the possibility of trust-based partnership, emotional security in the relationship, and two years of shared history, and you face the ongoing psychological cost of inhabiting doubt. The friend who reported the makeout stands to experience continued alienation from your partner based on an accusation she cannot reliably deny. The male acquaintance gains continued ambiguity about how his conduct will be characterized, insulating him from accountability. The broader friend group operates with fractured information and damaged trust.

3. DIRECTIVE: End the relationship. The decisive reason is that she has provided you three incompatible accounts (nothing happened; she slept over but it was innocent; she has blanks and cannot confirm her own actions) and has withheld material facts until forced disclosure, demonstrating that you cannot rely on her representations about her own conduct or her commitments to you.

[Rejected path: Attempt to establish the truth of the November encounter through further questioning. This produces an indefinite cycle of revision, reinterpretation, and your deepening investment in a narrative you can never verify; probability of primary harm: high.]

4. RECOMMENDATION: Terminate the partnership. The mechanism by which continued interrogation produces worse outcomes than separation is that each clarification she offers will be followed by either new information contradicting it or admission of further gaps in her memory, locking you into a position where you are perpetually gathering evidence of deception rather than deciding whether deception has occurred. She has already told you she engages in regrettable conduct while intoxicated and has a history of dishonesty in that state; her current inability to account for the night is not exculpatory. The fact that she is "brutally honest most of the time" is outweighed by the single decisive truth: when the stakes involve your explicitly stated vulnerability to infidelity, she chose concealment, late disclosure, and shifting accounts. Therefore: end this relationship immediately and do not re-enter it on the basis of a future clarification of what occurred.
